rationale: This record is a multi-book review essay discussing three macro-level books on economic growth, social development, bureaucracy and poverty in India. It does not address household or community water or sanitation service access (Criterion 1, E01), presents a book review rather than primary empirical evidence or a systematic review (Criterion 3, E05/E12), and reports no water or sanitation access outcomes (Criterion 4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although one of the reviewed books examines state bureaucracy broadly under the literal/plain wording of Criterion 2, no legal or administrative mechanism governing water or sanitation access is examined under the narrow reading, and both decisions remain exclude because Criteria 1, 3 and 4 fail.

evidence_quotes.quote: Book Review: Why Growth Matters: How Economic Growth in India Reduced Poverty and the Lessons for Other Developing Countries
Akhil Gupta, Red Tape: Bureaucracy, Structural Violence and Poverty in India. (Durham, Duke University Press, 2012)
